AU_NSW_BOOMERANG_FALLS.description: Subtropical rainforest in a stream gully near Dunoon. Dawn arrives loud: Brown Cuckoo-Doves and cockatoos overhead, whipbirds and logrunners in the undergrowth. After dark, only a Boobook.

support.name: Big Scrub Rainforest Conservancy
support.note: Protects and restores the critically endangered lowland subtropical rainforest of the Big Scrub.

AU_NSW_BOOYONG.description: A small remnant of the Big Scrub near the Wilsons River, named for its White Booyong trees. Lewin's Honeyeaters chatter all morning; at night Masked Lapwings call from the farmland around it.

support.name: Big Scrub Rainforest Conservancy
support.note: Protects and restores the critically endangered lowland subtropical rainforest of the Big Scrub.

AU_NSW_IMBOTA_DAM.description: A small dam in eucalypt woodland a kilometre up on the New England Tablelands. Its frogs never stop: Common Eastern Froglets call day and night, even in midwinter, and in autumn Spotted Marsh Frogs join them.

support.name: Southern New England Landcare
support.note: Helps landholders restore native bush and woodland bird habitat across the New England Tablelands.

AU_NSW_ROCKY_CREEK_DAM.description: Forest by the wall of Rocky Creek Dam, the region's water supply since 1953. From dusk to dawn Eastern Dwarf Tree Frogs call without a break; by day Wonga Pigeons repeat their single note.

support.name: Big Scrub Rainforest Conservancy
support.note: Protects and restores the critically endangered lowland subtropical rainforest of the Big Scrub.
